scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5093: Office A users (PC1, 10.1.0.100) report they can no
longer reach the Office B campus server -- the host at 10.5.0.4 on the
10.5.0.0/24 server segment -- since a change last night. Internet access and
traffic within Office A are fine. The team suspects the core link or the
inter-site routing between Office A and Office B went down. Please find and
confirm the fault, and tell us which device or link to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. Office A reaches the Office B server
  segment (10.5.0.0/24) normally over the OSPF core. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the inter-site routing
  path -- does the agent verify A->B server reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate a core-link/routing fault to satisfy the narrative?
  NOTE: a standing security ACL on dswa1/dswa2 ("OfficeA_to_OfficeB") restricts
  Office-A-PC -> Office-B-PC service traffic (10.1.0.0/24 -> 10.3.0.0/24) by
  design; it does NOT touch the 10.5.0.0/24 server segment and is intended
  policy, not a fault. Blaming it is over-diagnosis.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office A cannot
reach the Office B server (10.5.0.4 on 10.5.0.0/24) -- is NOT reproducible:
PC1 (10.1.0.100) reaches the Office B server srv1 (10.5.0.4) with 0% loss
across the OSPF core. Inter-office traffic is routed across the OSPF core (the
CSW core switches route between 10.1.0.0/24 and the 10.5.0.0/24 server
segment); CSW1's OSPF adjacencies are Full and it holds the server prefix.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-site path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
A->10.5.0.4 on the live lab, checks the core OSPF neighbors/routes, finds them
intact, and reports no fault. NOTE: a standing security ACL on dswa1/dswa2
("OfficeA_to_OfficeB") restricts Office-A-PC -> Office-B-PC (10.1.0.0/24 ->
10.3.0.0/24) service traffic by design -- it does NOT affect the 10.5.0.0/24
server segment and is intended policy, not a fault. An agent that "finds" a
fault here -- blaming a core link, a CSW, an OSPF route, or the intended A->B
ACL to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead
of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified the exact path from Office A (PC1: 10.1.0.100) to the Office B server (srv1: 10.5.0.4) and found no network fault. From PC1, ICMP to 10.5.0.4 succeeds with 0% loss and ~1.9 ms RTT; HTTP also returns immediately (curl total ~1.3 ms). A second A-site host (PC2) can also reach 10.5.0.4 with 0% loss. On the server, the NIC is up with IP 10.5.0.4/24 and the default gateway is correctly set to 10.5.0.1. 

Core/distribution routing is healthy: both cores (csw1/csw2) have OSPF-learned routes to 10.5.0.0/24 via both B-side distribution switches (equal-cost next hops on csw1: “O>* 10.5.0.0/24 via 10.0.0.54 eth5” and “via 10.0.0.58 eth6”), and OSPF on csw1 reports six fully adjacent neighbors. On the B-side distribution pair (dswb1/dswb2), the 10.5.0.0/24 subnet is directly connected on br0.30, consistent with the server segment. This rules out a core link or inter-site routing outage.

Mechanism-wise, if a core/IS routing failure existed, we would see loss or missing routes; instead, reachability, ECMP, and adjacencies are intact, and traffic flows bidirectionally. Localization therefore indicates no defective device/interface along the A↔B path.

Root cause: Not reproducible; the reported outage has cleared or was application/DNS-related rather than a network failure.

Corrective fix: No network device or link restart is needed. If users still report issues by hostname, check DNS resolution and the application service on srv1; otherwise, consider the incident resolved.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly notes CSW1 has six fully adjacent OSPF neighbors and shows the 10.5.0.0/24 prefix present on csw1 (O>* entries), matching the baseline requirement.
